claim: Open tape-guidance stack for AGVs: own CANopen sensor profile, ROS 2 driver and line follower.
limit: No real sensor or tape: profile, noise and timing are my assumptions, robot is a simple model.
alt: Dark plot of a tape layout with a fork, curve and two stop markers, and the paths a simulated robot drove along the tape to each marker.
post:
A tape-following robot is usually tested on the robot, so the hard cases (a fork, a stop marker, a dropped frame, a slow CAN gateway) are the hardest to repeat.

I built a magnetic-tape AGV guidance stack that runs without hardware: my own open CANopen profile for a tape guide sensor (frame layouts, fork, merge and marker flags, an object table), a simulator that emits it, a decoder library, a ROS 2 Jazzy driver and a line follower, closed in a loop with a simulated differential-drive robot.

Measured in simulation, 8 seeds: 0.83 mm median RMS tracking error, the right branch chosen 8 of 8 times, stops within 2.6 mm of the marker. Sweeps show where it breaks: stop accuracy fails at 200 ms of one-way latency, the junction choice at 300 ms, while 70% frame loss still gives about 1 mm RMS. In CI the same loop runs through the ROS 2 driver at 100 Hz.

Not verified: there is no real sensor or tape behind this. The profile, noise figures and channel timing are my assumptions, and the robot is a kinematic model without slip.

Which failure would you want to reproduce on a bench first: lost tape, a fork, or a late stop marker?

Code: https://github.com/VB-Builds/tape-guidance-lab
